about: Saved look sheets so the same character, place or region draws the same way every time. Every image prompt is built from these by composeImagePrompt(). 'canon' cites the Notion page a detail comes from; 'proposed' lists details Claude Code invented that James hasn't confirmed. Notion wins over this file.

style.prompt: Sword-and-sorcery comic art in the spirit of 1970s-80s Conan the Barbarian and Masters of the Universe: bold confident ink outlines, dramatic lighting, saturated flat colours with hard cel shading and halftone-dot shading, pulpy and dramatic. No text, no logos, no speech bubbles.
style.framing: Composition: a tight crop from the middle of a larger illustration, so the artwork runs off all four edges of the image. Nothing surrounds the art: no border, no white or cream margin, no paper, no frame, no panel outline.
style.emptySceneRule: Show only what is described. If no people or creatures are mentioned, the scene is empty of them: no figures, silhouettes or onlookers.
style.canon: Locked style prompt (Art Style Proofs, Round 8); art direction LOCKED on Presentation & Visuals.

delta.name: The Delta
delta.look: a permanent carnival that never packs up: raised plank boardwalks, timber-frame and clapboard buildings with tall flat painted false fronts like a frontier boomtown, striped canvas tents, rigging and bunting; gold leaf and grand columns only on a few permanent monuments. Hot, humid, lush river-delta air, hazy and damp.
delta.people: loud, colourful festival clothes; the rich wear the exotic beast trade: carved tusk pendants, coats made of tanned alligator hide, cloaks of huge impossible feathers. Everyone is human.
delta.canon: The Delta: Architecture: a permanent fairground (LOCKED); Biome; exotic creature trade (LOCKED).
proposed: hazy, damp light as the delta's visual signature

mage-city.name: Mage City
mage-city.look: a pale city on a flat-topped desert mesa: bone-white stone, sand-coloured fused glass and vitrified stone; sleek, flowing, curved towers in the spirit of Zaha Hadid that look too slender to stand, cantilevers over nothing, floating bridges and floating staircases hanging in mid-air between inward-facing towers; humble round mud-brick domes for the commoners at the mesa's foot.
mage-city.people: mages in long, layered robes of pale desert colours (bone, sand, sky blue) with tall stiff collars, every panel embroidered with diagrams and geometric script; commoners in plain undyed cotton and head-wraps.
mage-city.canon: Mage City: Architecture (LEANING), Hadid reference, floating stairs, commoner domes.

north.name: The North
north.look: make-do, never mastery: buildings are a patchwork of repairs, new timber lashed to old, hide over gaps; stone only for the lord's seat and military buildings. Trophies (antlers, furs, skulls), carved runes on lintels and beams, drying herbs and roots from rafters, bone charms by doors. Deep snow, glaciers and frozen lakes.
north.people: furs, leather, undyed wool and iron; long hair, braids and heavy beards; bone charms, beads and toggles; simple stark earned facial tattoos (lines, dots, lip-to-chin marks) on adults.
north.palette: dark browns, dark greys, black, undyed wool, raw leather, bone-white and antler-grey; nothing dyed.
north.canon: The North: Architecture, dress and the earned face (LOCKED); Terrain and wildlife (LEANING).

elves.name: Elves
elves.look: the elven plateau: a flat-topped tableland on a mountain range cradling a still sacred lake; architecture in the manner of Gaudí's Sagrada Família, carved stone that looks grown: porous honeycomb spires, bone and melting-candle-wax shapes, encrusted with stone fruit, shells and leaves, warm sandstone and bright mosaic tile; a Greek-style aqueduct and fountains; ornamental gardens and vineyards.
elves.people: humans changed by the water: human faces with long pointed ears, ageless and immaculate; exquisite, ornate court dress in the same organic language (flowing layers embroidered with shells, leaves and bone-like curves) in jewel tones.
never: plants or vines instead of carved stone
elves.canon: Elves (one kind of elf, no dark elves; Gaudí, LEANING); The Hoarded Fountain (born human; ears permanent, LOCKED/LEANING); Regions (plateau, lake, vineyards).

breadbasket.name: The breadbasket and the trade road
breadbasket.look: soft, flat farm country: grain fields, timber villages, the busiest trade road in the world with wagons and travellers streaming past.
breadbasket.people: plain medieval peasant and traveller clothes in wool and linen.

orcs.name: The orc badlands
orcs.look: cold volcanic badlands: black rock, grey ash plains, steam venting through snow, hot hostile ground under a freezing sky; open and exposed, no cover anywhere. Orc buildings are blunt and honest: rough volcanic stone, timber and stretched hide, with skulls and bones studded on as homemade decoration, wired on at slightly wrong angles, crooked and mismatched, a grinning uncle's trophy wall.
orcs.people: orcs, every one with the same grey-green skin: huge, broad, heavily muscled, heavy brows, small lower tusks, long coarse black hair often braided; open, expressive faces that beam easily. They wear hide, fur and leather, bone trinkets, and armour made from the hard shells and plates of badlands creatures (scorpion plates, dinosaur armour, arthropod shell) mixed with skulls and bones.
orcs.palette: black rock, ash grey, ember orange, snow white, bone, and the amber and rust of creature shell.
never: red, brown or bright green orc skin
humans in an orc crowd unless asked for
orcs.canon: Orc Badlands (cold volcanic badlands, LOCKED; wildlife, LEANING); Orcs (architecture and domestic culture, LOCKED; armour, LEANING).
proposed: orc bodies, skin, tusks and hair

dwarves.name: The dwarven mountains
dwarves.look: an alpine range of grey stone, dark pine forest and snow-capped peaks at the headwaters of a river. Dwarven architecture is beauty without ornament, in the spirit of Frank Lloyd Wright and Mies van der Rohe: long, clean horizontal slabs of stone cantilevered out of the living rock over open air, deep overhangs, bands of windows, crisp right angles, every surface plain and perfectly made; it is beautiful because it works, never because it is decorated.
dwarves.people: dwarves: short, broad, sturdy people with neat practical beards or braids, sleeves rolled up, leather work aprons and perfectly made plain work clothes in undyed and earthy tones, always busy at a task; any armour is plain, smooth, polished steel plate with no decoration. Human and other traders come and go, buying and selling, then leaving.
dwarves.palette: pale grey granite, warm honey-coloured stone, the green of planted terraces, white water, snow and dark pine.
never: fantasy dwarf halls with pillars and braziers
dwarves.canon: Dwarven Mountains (live on the face, beauty without ornament, form follows function, the Fallingwater gate; all LOCKED); Regions (alpine range, pine, snow; headwaters of one river); Dwarves (plain white-harness armour). Dwarves: The economy (the mountain is a trade hub, a place of transaction not revelry, LOCKED).
proposed: dwarf bodies, faces and everyday clothing

emperor.name: The self-crowned emperor
emperor.body: a heavy, soft, bloated human man of about fifty, jowly with several chins, always sweating
emperor.face: flushed cheeks, small nervous eyes that dart sideways, thinning oiled dark hair, clean-shaven, a greasy shine
emperor.outfit: a cloth-of-gold robe under a heavy fur mantle, heaps of gold chains, a ring on every finger, a carved tusk pendant
emperor.props: his self-commissioned crown: brand-new gold made to look ancient, far too big, studded with too many jewels, never sitting quite straight
emperor.canon: The Emperor's Crown: His look ('a much less extreme Jabba the Hutt', LOCKED), the crown (LOCKED), Opening State (he still has the crown).
proposed: age, hair, clean-shaven, cloth-of-gold robe, tusk pendant

mazirian.name: Mazirian, the vain councillor
mazirian.body: a tall, lean, very upright man in his sixties
mazirian.face: sharp handsome features gone haughty, nose raised, a short neatly trimmed silver beard, immaculate swept-back silver hair
mazirian.outfit: the most elaborate robes in the room: bone-white and gold, with a towering stiff embroidered collar and gold diagrams stitched over every panel; crystal rings
mazirian.canon: Mage City: The High Council (the vain one, Mazirian; three councillors).

proceduralist.name: The proceduralist (name OPEN)
proceduralist.body: a small, plump, neat woman in her sixties
proceduralist.face: tight grey bun, a pursed, polite little smile, round spectacles on a chain
proceduralist.outfit: prim high-necked robes in dove grey with tiny embroidered seals down the front; always holding a ribbon-tied scroll and a quill
proceduralist.canon: Mage City: The High Council (female proceduralist, Umbridge touchstone held at arm's length).

rimwald.name: Rimwald, the zoned-out councillor
rimwald.body: a very old, frail, stooped man
rimwald.face: bald with wisps of white hair, a long untidy white beard, heavy-lidded drowsy eyes
rimwald.outfit: faded sea-green robes worn slightly askew, collar crooked
rimwald.canon: Mage City: The High Council (Rimwald, detached, half-asleep).

skin-witch.name: The skin witch (name OPEN)
skin-witch.body: in human form, a small, kindly old woman, slightly stooped
skin-witch.face: soft round face with deep smile lines, long grey braids, faded earned tattoo lines on the chin
skin-witch.outfit: fur-trimmed undyed wool, a leather apron hung with herb pouches and bone charms
skin-witch.trueForm: under the skin, a towering chimera of mismatched human and animal parts fused by raw, wet, pale flesh: several human arms of different sizes and skin tones, a goat's leg, a mouth in its chest full of tongues, an extra jaw, a few tentacles, joints bending the wrong way
skin-witch.canon: The Skin Witch (LEANING): chimera under a human skin; village healer as conspirator is a Claude proposal James liked. The Honest God & Witchcraft: chimera flesh.
proposed: that the witch is an old woman

prison-guard.name: A prison guard
prison-guard.body: an ordinary human local, a paid shift worker, not a soldier
prison-guard.outfit: crown-issued plain kit: a padded gambeson, a plain iron cap, a heavy ring of keys; a real sword or mace at the belt
prison-guard.canon: Story: Guards, arming (human, crown-issued, lethal weapons; LEANING).

prison-chaplain.name: The prison chaplain (the town priest)
prison-chaplain.body: a modest, ordinary middle-aged village priest
prison-chaplain.outfit: a plain dark parish cassock, a simple wooden prayer token on a cord
prison-chaplain.canon: Story: the parish priest doubles as the prison's chaplain (James); sincere, numbed or troubled is OPEN.

orc-armourer.name: The orc armour-maker
orc-armourer.body: an enormous old orc smith, scarred forearms like tree trunks
orc-armourer.face: grey-green skin, small chipped tusks, a braided grey beard, a huge earnest proud grin
orc-armourer.outfit: a scorched leather apron over bare arms, his own pauldron of scorpion plate, bone toggles in his braids

openingOutfits.about: The player and cellmates wake in their own plain peasant clothes, stripped of anything useful, loosely flavoured by archetype (Story: What you're wearing, James). Bodies and faces come from the player, not this file.
openingOutfits.warrior: sturdy work clothes: a thick wool tunic, a scuffed leather jerkin with its buckles cut away, heavy trousers, bare feet or worn boots with no laces
openingOutfits.rogue: a close-fitting, worn dark tunic and a frayed hood, soft patched boots
openingOutfits.mage: a plain undyed woollen robe tied with a rope belt
proposed: all three outfits beyond 'sturdier work clothes' and 'a plain woollen robe' (Claude examples on Story)

delta-joust.name: The arrival joust
delta-joust.look: an open-air jousting list on the Strip: a sanded lane split by a wooden tilt rail, plank boardwalk stands packed with spectators, painted false fronts and striped tents behind, pennants and bunting overhead

mage-city-skyline.name: The mage city from the desert
mage-city-skyline.look: the whole city seen from the desert floor: pale mesa, flowing bone-white towers, at least three floating staircases with no supports, floating bridges, and at the centre the High Council's ornate building with a smooth seamless face and no door, window or opening of any kind; humble mud-brick domes tiny at the foot of the cliffs; empty desert to the horizon
mage-city-skyline.canon: Mage City: Architecture (LEANING), responsive entrance-less council building.

council-chamber.name: The High Council chamber
council-chamber.look: a bright, pale chamber with smooth curving white walls of fused glass and bone-coloured stone, flowing like Zaha Hadid architecture, lit by daylight from above; a high curved bench for three; the orb on a stone plinth in the middle of the floor
council-chamber.canon: The Oracle Orb (orb on a plinth, session-only).

elven-plateau.name: The elven plateau
elven-plateau.look: the plateau seen from the air: sheer cliffs rooted to the mountain range, the sacred lake in the middle, Gaudí stone spires around it, an aqueduct feeding fountains, terraced vineyards; lower on the mountainside, in haze, the separate church city on the flank
elven-plateau.canon: Regions (plateau, endorheic lake; holy city on the flank, LOCKED); The Hoarded Fountain (aqueduct).

great-hall.name: A northern great hall
great-hall.look: a great hall built by people with no carpenters: crude, uneven, improvised. Walls are a patchwork of planks of different widths, ages and colours, some charred; new pale timber lashed with rope to old blackened beams; animal hides nailed over holes; daylight and snow showing through gaps; stone only at the base. A long central fire pit is the only warmth. One whole wall is a smoke-darkened timber board carved top to bottom with rows of runic names: the wall of names
great-hall.canon: The North (make-do, great hall with central fire, LOCKED); The North Rebellion (wall of names, LOCKED).

rooted-city.name: The rooted city
rooted-city.look: a vast underground city in a cavern: streets and tiers of buildings made of brass-and-iron machinery (gears, pistons, pipes, great clockwork engines) receding into the distance, all half-swallowed by pale roots, vines and furred grey fungus; faint lights still glow; a few gears still turn
rooted-city.canon: Combustion: The dungeon: the rooted city; the cold open (LEANING).

witch-den.name: The skin witch's den
witch-den.look: a low, torchlit den of rough timber and stone, drying herbs and bone charms hanging from the beams, and a ring of carved northern runes on the floor

prison-cell.name: The cell
prison-cell.look: a small cell for three, about three by two and a half metres, at ground level: rough undressed fieldstone walls in lime mortar, damp stone flags on the floor, a timber beam-and-plank ceiling; a heavy iron-banded timber door with a small barred grille at head height and a food hatch below it; a timber plank shelf with old straw along one wall, more straw on the floor; a wooden water jug and a slop bucket; one narrow barred slit window high on the outer wall letting in a blade of daylight
never: walls or doors made of iron bars
prison-cell.canon: Story: The cell: daily routine and contents (LEANING; size, walls, window are Claude proposals James approved).

cell-block.name: The cell block
cell-block.look: a long, single-storey stone hall at ground level, a row of heavy timber cell doors with small grilles down one side, a timber ceiling, daylight from high slit windows
cell-block.canon: Story: The prison itself; The interior (LEANING).

prison-exterior.name: The prison on the trade road
prison-exterior.look: a long, low, single-storey stone building with a timber roof and one gate, plain and purely functional, the one hard stone thing in soft farm country; the busiest trade road in the world runs past it, crowded with wagons and travellers; a small timber town (cottages, an inn with a stable, a parish church with a graveyard) clusters around it among grain fields
prison-exterior.canon: Story: Where the prison sits; The prison itself; Guards, arming, the prison town (LEANING).

orc-village.name: An orc settlement
orc-village.look: an orc settlement on black volcanic rock: squat, blunt houses of rough volcanic stone, timber and stretched hide; skulls and bones studded on as decoration and infill, wired on at wrong angles, a skull wedged into a wall where a rock would have done; a skull used as a flower vase in a window, a ribcage used as an herb-drying rack, a femur for a door handle; steam venting through snow between the houses, ash underfoot

orc-hearth.name: Inside an orc home
orc-hearth.look: inside an orc home: rough volcanic-stone walls hung with a few honoured trophy skulls, a big fire pit, hides and furs on the floor, a giant creature shell used as a tub, shoulder-blade bones used as serving platters, a skull on the table holding wildflowers; warm, cosy and cluttered
orc-hearth.canon: Orcs: Architecture and domestic culture (LOCKED); Armour (shells as bathtubs and bowls).

ash-plain.name: The ash plains
ash-plain.look: open badlands: black rock and grey ash plains to the horizon, steam venting through patches of snow, distant smoking volcanoes, a freezing grey sky, no cover anywhere

dwarf-face.name: The sunward face of the dwarven mountains
dwarf-face.look: the whole sunward face of a great mountain, seen from across the valley. The homes are hundreds of plain rectangular stone blocks stacked and offset up the slope in the spirit of Habitat 67: each block shifted from the one below so that every roof is the garden of the home above, blocks bridging and cantilevering over each other, open-air walkways and stairs threading between them, bands of glass windows. Every rooftop garden grows food in perfectly straight rows: cabbages, beans climbing poles, herbs, squash, espaliered fruit trees, beehives. Below and between the homes, tier after tier of green barley terraces cascade down the slope. In the centre a huge waterfall pours out of the rock, and the great gate is ONE great building over and into it, the boldest, most daring structure on the mountain: long, wide horizontal stone floors cantilevered far out across the falling water like Fallingwater made monumental, in the same clean style as the homes. Stone channels carry water from the falls across the terraces and turn the waterwheels of forges, whose smoke rises from neat openings in the cliff. At the mountain's foot, where the falls become a navigable river: a crowded, bustling river harbour: dozens of flat river barges moored three deep along long, plain, perfectly cut stone quays and more queuing midstream to dock; a whole row of precise counterweighted timber-and-steel cranes swinging cargo at once; warehouses with wide square doorways cut straight into the cliff base; rail tracks running along the quays with loaded carts; streams of dwarf dockworkers, porters and clerks with ledgers, and traders from every region haggling briskly; wine barrels, baskets of fish, sacks of grain, timber and bales arriving from across the world, and crates of plain polished steel armour and swords going out. Busy, orderly and businesslike: no tavern, no stalls, no revelry. The river runs on through pine forest toward the distant lowlands; snow-capped peaks above
dwarf-face.canon: Dwarven Mountains: They live on the face (planted roofs, terraced farms, waterfall irrigation driving the forges), The establishing shot (LOCKED); Habitat 67 and food-growing rooftop gardens (James, 2026-11-03); the river harbour (James, 2026-11-03), built on Dwarves: The economy (LOCKED) and Regions (headwaters of one river, metalwork floating down to the delta).
never: thin walkways in place of the gate

dwarf-harbour.name: The dwarven river harbour
dwarf-harbour.look: the dwarven river harbour at the foot of the mountains, where the falls become a navigable river: a crowded, bustling port: dozens of flat river barges moored three deep along long, plain, perfectly cut stone quays and more queuing midstream to dock; a whole row of precise counterweighted timber-and-steel cranes swinging cargo at once; warehouses with wide square doorways cut straight into the cliff base; rail tracks running along the quays with loaded carts; streams of dwarf dockworkers, porters and clerks with ledgers, and traders from every region haggling briskly; wine barrels, baskets of fish, sacks of grain, timber and bales arriving from across the world, and crates of plain polished steel armour and swords going out. Busy, orderly and businesslike: no tavern, no stalls, no revelry. Above, the stacked Habitat 67-style homes climb the cliff with food gardens on every roof, and the great waterfall thunders down beside the harbour
dwarf-harbour.canon: Dwarves: The economy (trade hub of transaction, not revelry; no tavern; LOCKED); Regions (river carries their metalwork down to the delta). The harbour itself: James, 2026-11-03.
